lead_time_analysis.stability: Unstable — high CV (0.63); bimodal distribution with short (~1 day) and medium (~3 day) clusters

narrative: Material PL1__M017F74F shows moderate demand variability (CV=0.49) across 139 working days with a mild declining trend, and a bimodal lead time distribution (short ~1 day and medium ~3 day clusters) resulting in an unstable CV of 0.63. Lead time variance dominates the safety buffer at 73.5%, driving a required safety stock of 913 units to achieve the 95% service level target. The unconstrained EOQ of 17,161 units exceeds the storage limit of 6,925 units, so an (r,Q) policy with a storage-capped order quantity of 6,012 units and reorder point of 2,148 units is recommended. The SAP safety lead time of 4.0 days overstates actual variability; a reduction to 2.01 days is advised.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint active: EOQ (17161) capped to 6012 units (max_storage_units 6925 minus safety_stock 913).
Current SAP safety stock is 0 — material is fully exposed to stockout risk under current policy.
Declining demand trend detected (slope ~-1.59 units/day); EOQ and safety stock should be reviewed quarterly.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) — Continuous Review Reorder Point / Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is moderately variable but largely continuous (93.5% non-zero days), making a continuous review (r,Q) policy appropriate. The bimodal lead time distribution requires explicit safety stock rather than relying on safety lead time alone. EOQ provides the cost-optimal order quantity subject to the storage cap and MOQ constraints.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds hard: the economically optimal EOQ of 17,161 units is ~2.5× the storage limit. Capping to 6,012 units increases ordering frequency from ~7 orders/year to ~18 orders/year, raising annual ordering costs by roughly 2.5× versus unconstrained EOQ. If storage capacity can be expanded, significant cost savings are achievable.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (1483) + safety_stock (913) = 2396, which is below max_storage_units (6925). Policy is feasible. No MOQ-capacity conflict.
